propositions: run_git_write does not retry write-side temp-file creation faults (unable to create temporary file, failed to insert into database, unable to index file) because _with_transient_head_retry only matches READ-side markers (could not parse head, bad object)

event_append._git_add path retries the same write-side faults via _with_transient_add_retry, but other callers (s3_doctor, compaction, claim/transition writers) using run_git_write lack this protection, creating asymmetric failure modes

s3_doctor test test_heal_folds_into_the_ref_from_a_detached_head_tracker failed with S3DoctorConflict on one CI shard when git commit-tree encountered unable to create temporary file error, indicating a runner-FS transient fault that would self-heal on the event_append path but aborts on the shared seam
Moving _TRANSIENT_WRITE_MARKERS and its predicate into gitutil as a shared definition unifies the retry logic so all run_git_write callers inherit the bounded 3-attempt write-side fault retry

The fix renames _with_transient_head_retry to _with_transient_fault_retry and _is_transient_head_error to _is_transient_git_fault because the retry loop now handles both READ and WRITE faults, and collapses the accidental nested 3x3 attempt budget on commit paths to the intended bounded 3
Corrupt-object signatures (loose object is corrupt, inflate: data stream error) remain excluded from retry; genuine persistent faults still surface immediately after budget exhaustion
